subject: Oceanography
title: Geography of the Arctic
description: A micro-lesson that makes Geography of the Arctic usable.

hook.text: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest ocean—almost entirely surrounded by land.

buildup.text: It covers 14.06 million km² and is connected to the Pacific by the narrow Bering Strait.

discovery.text: The Lomonosov Ridge splits the ocean in two—a mountain range rising 3,000 m from the seafloor beneath the ice.

twist.text: Unlike Antarctica, the Arctic has no continent—it's an ocean covered by floating ice, not land beneath it.

climax.text: Five nations border the Arctic Ocean—and all are competing for its resources as ice retreats.

punchline.text: The smallest ocean hides the biggest geopolitical contest.

quiz.question: What lies beneath the Arctic ice?
